paragraphs.text: A cake of [ripe pu’er](shou:definition) from Menghai in Yunnan, sold under the name Pasha and pressed in 2015. Before pressing, the leaf was heaped warm and damp in a [fermenting pile](shou:wet-piling), the method Yunnan’s state factories took into production in 1973.
At eleven years the cake has crossed into what the trade counts as [aged ripe pu’er](shou:age-aged). From here, how it is stored shapes it as much as the years do.

brewing.text: Ease a piece off the cake along its edge with a pick rather than snapping it. Use boiling water, about 7 grams to 100 ml, one quick rinse, then short steeps that lengthen as the leaf opens. It gives eight or more good cups.

notice.text: A deep cup with woody, date-like or medicinal notes, which the trade calls aged aroma.
